paragraphs: Ranger Mark Changes the Notice, posted by Lily. Next Saturday, the Explorers will have an outdoor day in the nature park. The park is quiet in the morning, so many animals come out. We will go riding in the morning, and we will swim in the lake in the afternoon. Leo wrote a notice for the day. Ranger Mark read it and gave us advice. Then he wrote a new version. Here are both versions, so you can find the differences.

This is the notice of Leo, the first version. He wrote it in two minutes with a blue marker. The title says, "Outdoor Day in the Park." The first line says, "Ride your bike on all the paths." The second line says, "Swim in the lake after lunch." The next line says, "You can dive from the big rock." The last line says, "Bring a helmet and a bottle of water."

This is the notice of Ranger Mark, the second version. The title says, "Outdoor Day in the Park." The first line says, "Ride your bike only on the park road." The second line says, "Swim in the lake after lunch, with a ranger." The next line says, "Do not dive from the big rock." The last line says, "Bring a helmet and a bottle of water."

The two notices have three differences. The first is the place for the bikes. Ranger Mark's advice is helpful, because bikes on small paths are loud for the wildlife. Many animals live near the paths, and they need quiet. Leo listened carefully, and he did not say a word. The second is the ranger at the lake, because the water is deep in some places. The last is the dive. The water near the rock is not deep, so a dive is a danger.

After the changes, Leo was not upset. "The new notice is better," he said. He drew a small bike and a small fish on it. A good notice keeps people and animals safe. Mia asked, "Can we ride to the lake together?" "Yes, on the park road," said Ranger Mark with a smile.
An outdoor day is fun, and it is good exercise. This area of the park is a home for many animals. So we must be quiet, careful, and kind. Which notice do you like more?
text.summary: Lily shows two versions of a notice for an outdoor day in the nature park. Leo wrote the first one, and Ranger Mark gave advice and changed three parts to keep the wildlife and the children safe.
